clue.text: Souvenir found outside inn by an adherent of McKinley?

indicators.note: the souvenir word is found wrapped around the inn word, so one sits outside the other

parts.note: a relic is a keepsake or souvenir
a pub is an inn
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone buys a keepsake outside a pub and is revealed as a fan of an old American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found outside' puts RELIC around PUB to give REPUBLIC, then AN follows. William McKinley was a US President from the Republican Party, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: McKinley led the Republican Party as US President, so a follower of his politics belongs to that party.

clue.text: Boulder seen to sway from side to side

definitions.meaning: to move gently to and fro, as a cradle does

explanation.surface: A large stone appears to wobble back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulder is a large stone, and to sway back and forth is to move like a cradle being tipped.

clue.text: Price of drink raised? It causes a fight

definitions.meaning: punch, the bowl drink, put up in price, read whimsically
a brawl with fists, read loosely as the thing that sets one off

explanation.surface: A barman puts the cost of a drink up, and the regulars come to blows over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch is a mixed drink, so raising it is a cryptic reading; a brawl or fistfight is also called this.

clue.text: Literary woman in indecent close-fitting garment

parts.note: blue means risqué or smutty, as in blue jokes
a stocking is a tight garment for the leg

explanation.surface: A woman of letters is shocked to find herself in a racy piece of hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: A bluestocking is an old term for an intellectual or literary woman, from an 18th-century London salon.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was coined for learned women of an 18th-century salon and still describes a scholarly female intellectual.

clue.text: Certain characters, sort of square, have a reciprocal effect

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, so the letters of certain are sorted into a new order

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square

explanation.surface: Some sort of square-shaped figures seem to influence each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges CERTAIN into INTERAC; 'characters' just says letters are being used. T follows, from the T-square of technical drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: When two things act upon each other mutually, each influences the other in return.

clue.text: A free broadcasting organization, it's commonly said

parts.note: to untie something is to set it free

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is described as free of charge by popular opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE is the affectionate nickname for the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster; 'it's commonly said' marks it as informal.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is popularly nicknamed this as a fussy, motherly relative figure among British broadcasters.

clue.text: Grecian eminence used to being put upon

definitions.meaning: a mountain in Greece, eminence meaning high ground
in the myth Mount Pelion was heaped on top of this peak

explanation.surface: A Greek dignitary is accustomed to being taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piling Pelion on Ossa' is a classical phrase for heaping one difficulty on another.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a mountain in Thessaly, and in myth the giants piled Pelion upon it to storm heaven.

clue.text: Amount of' money enclosed can't possibly build a holy place

indicators.note: the cash total is said to enclose the other letters, so it goes round them

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of can't could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pile of cash is locked away but still cannot pay for a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns CANT into ANCT, which 'enclosed' places inside SUM. The stray apostrophe after 'of' is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a sacred inner chamber of a temple or church.

clue.text: In which we're in the nude, entirely

definitions.text: In which we're in the nude

explanation.surface: A naturist explains what being completely naked means.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In the altogether' is an idiom for naked, and the word also means wholly or completely.

clue.text: Top specialist becomes state agent — so much for the French!

parts.note: a consul is an official representing a state abroad
tant is French for so much

explanation.surface: A leading expert turns diplomat and dismisses France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so much for the French' looks like a dismissive aside, but it asks for French 'so much', TANT. In Britain a consultant is the most senior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals the most senior doctor in a specialty holds this title.

clue.text: Difficult problem for a wader

definitions.meaning: a tangle, something hard to unravel
a shorebird of the sandpiper family

explanation.surface: A wading bird faces a tricky puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a tangle hard to undo, and the knot is a sandpiper-like shorebird.

clue.text: He is quick to fire a sucker taken in by a swindler

indicators.note: the sucker is taken inside the swindler's word, so it sits within it

parts.note: a sharper is a cheat or card swindler
a sucker is a shoot growing from a plant's root

explanation.surface: A gullible person is conned by a crook, while someone else is trigger-happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' looks like a dupe for the swindler, but it is the botanical sense: a shoot. 'taken in by' puts SHOOT inside SHARPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is skilled at firing accurately, and readily so.

clue.text: Some inhabitants of Corinth used it in this way

indicators.note: the answer lives among the letters of the following words, as some of their residents

explanation.surface: Certain residents of an ancient Greek city made use of something like this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means so, or in this manner.

clue.text: Its charge exploded — it was fired in Berlin

indicators.note: blowing up the letters scatters them into a new order

explanation.surface: An explosive charge goes off and a famous building in Berlin is set alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' rearranges ITS CHARGE. The German parliament building burned in 1933.
explanation.definitionFit: The German parliament building in Berlin was gutted by fire in 1933.

clue.text: String of flowers for girl cyclist on links

parts.note: Daisy is the girl in the song about a bicycle made for two
a chain is made of links

explanation.surface: A garland of blooms is made for a young woman who cycles on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' suggests a golf course but means chain links. The Victorian song 'Daisy Bell' features a bicycle built for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Children thread wild flowers together stem to stem to make such a garland.

clue.text: Make tentative proposal to a very quiet swimmer

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quietly
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone gently suggests something to a shy swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound someone out with an overture is to make advances toward them.

clue.text: Acting with alacrity to assist the speaker

definitions.meaning: to give a forgotten line to someone on stage

explanation.surface: On stage, someone quickly helps a performer who has forgotten lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means quick or punctual, and also to feed lines to a forgetful actor.

clue.text: Animal some order in the market

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are put inside the market word

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: putting the letters of some in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A creature restores some order at a busy trading place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges SOME into MOSE, which 'in' places inside MART.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: Collide with second vehicle

parts.note: a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: Two vehicles crash, the second one hitting the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit or crash into something.

clue.text: A possible barrier to vituperation

explanation.surface: Something might stand in the way of an angry tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of bars is a barrier, and ranting abuse is to rail against someone.

clue.text: Indiscriminate slaughter in US and Brazilian states

parts.note: Mass is the short form of Massachusetts, a US state
Acre is a state in western Brazil

explanation.surface: Mass killing has occurred in parts of the United States and Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' and 'Brazilian' each qualify 'states': one state from each country.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesale killing of many people at once.

clue.text: Eccentric deal, perhaps, for a source of dye

parts.note: an eccentric is a disc or cam turning off-centre on a shaft
deal is pine or fir timber, an example of wood

explanation.surface: An odd bargain is struck over where some colouring comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' and 'deal' read as an odd bargain; they are the engineering eccentric (a cam) and deal timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Camwood is a West African tree whose red heartwood yields dye.

clue.text: Lemur eating a farinaceous tuber

indicators.note: the animal eats the letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: the potto is a slow-moving African primate related to lemurs

explanation.surface: A lemur is munching a starchy root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts A inside POTTO. Farinaceous means starchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The spud is the classic starchy underground tuber.

clue.text: Stone or, ring mislaid in river

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the river name

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: mislaid suggests the letters have been put down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone has lost a stone or a ring in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' rearranges OR RING into IRNGOR, which 'in' places inside CAM. The comma after 'or' is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairngorm is a smoky yellow-brown quartz gem from the Scottish mountains of that name.

clue.text: Resistance units serving the monarch?

definitions.meaning: the initials of On His or Her Majesty's Service, printed on official British mail

explanation.surface: Members of the Resistance are working for the king.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance, and OHMS is short for On Her Majesty's Service.

clue.text: Formerly the last word in fairytales? Quite the opposite

definitions.meaning: at some time in the past

definitions.text: the last word in fairytales? Quite the opposite
definitions.meaning: the first word of a fairytale, not the last

explanation.surface: Fairy stories used to end with a certain word, but in truth it is the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at one time, and opens fairytales as 'Once upon a time'.

clue.text: A soccer team's. league

parts.note: a soccer team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals, with the 's giving S

explanation.surface: A football club belongs to a league.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a common way of naming a team; the 's adds S. The stray full stop after team's is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War.

clue.text: Advantage handy at first in instinctive music-maker

indicators.note: the advantage and the initial go inside the word for instinctive

parts.note: born, as in a born musician, means having a natural instinct
an asset is an advantage

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of handy

explanation.surface: Someone with a natural gift finds it handy to have an edge at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ASSET plus H inside BORN. A basset horn is an alto clarinet.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset horn is a woodwind instrument of the clarinet family, used by Mozart.

clue.text: Endless darkness is near

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: Unending darkness is approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Close at hand, an old word for close by.

clue.text: Game to follow infantry in river crossing, perhaps

indicators.note: the game is said to follow the infantry, so it comes after it

parts.note: foot soldiers, the foot, are infantry
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A match is played after foot soldiers cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shows a footbridge need not cross a river; it might span a road or railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow bridge for pedestrians, which may span water.
